text:
maya: Heads-up — while running nightly MoE perf sweep on the 8xA100 cluster I hit a nasty hotspot during token routing. end-to-end latency jumped 2.7x on long-context traces.

oliver: Ugh, saw something similar in the canary yesterday. Is the all-to-all step spiking or the post-routing softmax?

maya: Profiling points to an all-to-all imbalance — a few ranks spend way more time in `AllToAll` and then wait on reductions. nvprof summary: `alltoall: 52%`, `matmul: 18%`, `cudaMemcpy: 12%`.

choi: Can you paste the trace snippet? curious if it's network saturation or serialization due to small messages.

maya: Paste below — this is tail of timeline for a high-token session (seq_len 8192, batch 4, MoE 32 experts):
```
[rank0] AllToAll send  6.8ms  recv wait 3.1ms
[rank1] AllToAll send 29.1ms recv wait 0.2ms
[rank2] AllToAll send 5.5ms  recv wait 4.2ms
[rank3] AllToAll send 4.9ms  recv wait 5.1ms
... skew: rank1 is the slow path
```

oliver: Looks like token fanout skew — some ranks get way more tokens for certain prompts. Did you try the routing cap heuristic?

maya: Yeah. We tried `router.max_tokens_per_expert=1024` but it only reduced tail by ~10%. The underlying issue seems to be that expert assignment for our token distribution has high variance for this workload.

choi: Two angles: (1) reduce fragmentation by increasing batch packing window so we aggregate more tokens before routing, (2) make the all-to-all use larger message sizes to amortize startup. Have you tried increasing `comm_buffer_size` in the runtime?

maya: I bumped `comm_buffer_size` from 128KB -> 1MB and reran. AllToAll time median dropped 18% but the skew persisted. packing window helps latency but hurts memory pressure.

profiler-bot: New profile uploaded: s3://profiles/nightly/1779504321/maya/moe-sweep.tar.gz

oliver: Can we try a micro-benchmark that simulates the same expert distribution but with synthetic tensors to isolate NIC vs compute? If all-ranks show similar send sizes but one rank slower, network is suspect.

maya: Good call. I ran a synthetic `alltoall_bench.py` using the exact per-expert counts from the trace. Result: rank1 still slower by ~3.6x on message setup time. Kernel timings show `ncclGroupStart`/`ncclAllToAll` overhead high on that node.

choi: Is the node the same GPU model/firmware? Could be PCIe link differences or driver jitter. Also double-check process placement — is a heavy IO daemon on that host?

maya: Node is A100-80GB same firmware. There was a backup job on rank1 host earlier, but I thought it completed. I'll repro on isolated nodes.

oliver: In parallel, let's try software mitigations: (A) shard routing table so hot experts are split across two physical ranks, (B) add a quick local fallback: if an expert assignment would exceed X tokens, spill to the next-expert in the list and penalize score slightly. That reduces prime skew at the cost of slightly different routing.

maya: Implemented a simple spill heuristic in router: `if tokens_assigned[expert] + n > cap -> pick second_best`. Ran on canary, tail latency reduced ~30% and mean improved 12%. Quality tests show negligible perplexity diff (<0.02).

choi: Great. We should also check kernel selection for the expert forward path — when routing is skewed, some ranks do a ton of small GEMMs. If we switch to a batched-GEMM kernel for small matrices it can win. Any kernel autotune logs?

maya: Autotuner picked `cutlass_small_gemm_v2` for sizes <64 and `cutlass_large` otherwise. But when load spikes, we have hundreds of tiny GEMMs which create host->device launches. I prototyped a micro-batching combiner: group small expert tensors into a single batched GEMM call. That reduced kernel launch overhead by ~40% in the bench.

oliver: Nice. Combine that with the spill heuristic and larger comm buffers and we might get consistent perf. Any regression vs throughput when doing micro-batching?

maya: Throughput improved for skewed sessions; for uniform distribution it's neutral. Memory overhead is small (~5%).

choi: Action items: 1) maya to run isolated node repro and collect NIC counters (iperf, ethtool stats) — due EOD. 2) oliver to draft a router rollout plan with spill heuristic toggle and metrics gating. 3) maya to add micro-batching flag behind runtime opt-in. 4) infra to check for background jobs on rank1 host.

maya: Filed infra ticket: #INF-2187 — noted the host. Uploading NIC counters to the profile bundle now.

profiler-bot: Workflow note: schedule perf regression alert if p95 latency increases >20% on MoE routes after rollout.

oliver: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow morning with the infra folks. If the isolated repro shows network as cause, we can avoid router-level compromises.

maya: Agree. For now I'll keep the spill heuristic behind a flag and add metrics for token skew per-expert so we can alert when distribution variance > threshold. :white_check_mark:

choi: Solid. Also add a small test in our perf harness that injects worst-case expert skew to catch future regressions.

maya: Will do. I'll post links to the synthetic bench and the patch in this thread when ready.

oliver: Perfect — appreciate the quick turnaround on this. :rocket:
